The initial probe reports the best transform per view — and the chosen signs differ between views 0 and 1 ([1,-1,-1,-1] vs [-1,1,-1,-1]), suggesting no single shared signed permutation may fit, which would violate the contract's shared (p, s) requirement. The probe never computes the shared E.

message.reasoning_content: The kernel sorts columns per-view by anchor magnitude — meaning permutation can differ per view. Initial probe found view 0 best permutation [0,2,1,3] with signs [1,-1,-1,-1] and view 1 same permutation but signs [-1,1,-1,-1] — different signs per view! That's view-dependent, violating the shared-transform contract. Initial probe passes per-view but the contract requires a single shared (p,s). So the key risk: per-view transforms satisfy E only if a shared transform exists. Whether a shared transform fits is an open question — anchor signs differ per view, so sign of columns likely differs across views. Need experiments (shared E computation).
